topics.title: Using the t-formula to solve equations

questions.hint: Set t = tan(2θ) and use the double-angle formulas. Solve the quadratic, then list every 2θ value in [0, 2π] before halving.

keyPoints.note: For a 4θ equation, the substitution \(t=\tan2\theta\) makes the double-\angle formulas quadratic.

steps.explain: Use the double-angle formulas for 4θ. The original equation has no solutions with cos(2θ)=0, so divide by cos²(2θ) and set t = tan(2θ).
Substitute and solve the resulting quadratic.
Map both tangent values into the full interval 0≤2θ≤2π.
Divide each 2θ value by 2 and check that all four angles satisfy 0≤θ≤π.

questions.stem: A school schedules 2733 classes over 40 periods in a fortnight. By the pigeonhole principle, what is the minimum number of classrooms that guarantees each class can have a separate room?
questions.hint: Divide the total number of classes by the number of periods and round up to the next whole room.

keyPoints.note: The average number of classes per period gives a lower bound; take the ceiling.
Focus on this information when choosing the method.

steps.explain: Find the average number of classes scheduled per period.
The number of classrooms must be a whole number. Round the average up to guarantee enough rooms in the busiest period.
Thus the minimum guaranteed classroom count is 69.

questions.stem: A school schedules 2733 classes over 40 periods. The pigeonhole principle gives a minimum guaranteed classroom count. Why might that count still fail to provide a separate room for every class in every period?
options: The classes may be distributed unevenly, so one period can contain more than the average number.
The average must be rounded down.
Rooms can only be used in alternate periods.
The number of periods changes the number of classes.
questions.hint: The pigeonhole principle gives a guaranteed lower bound based on the average, not the exact largest period.

keyPoints.note: Think about whether the 2733 classes are evenly spread across all 40 periods.

keyPoints.text: Why might that count still fail
keyPoints.note: Focus on this information when choosing the method.

steps.explain: The quotient \(2733/40=68.325\) is an average, not the exact number of classes in every period.
If classes are unevenly distributed, one period can exceed the average.
Therefore the guarantee based on the average may not meet the busiest period.

questions.solution: The classes may be distributed unevenly, so one period can contain more than the average number.
